approachQuestion.prompt: An expression is either an integer or SUB(left,right), meaning the left value minus the right value. Return its value. Examples: SUB(10,SUB(7,2)) returns 5; SUB(SUB(10,7),2) returns 1; -4 returns -4.
constraints: The expression is a finite tree with n objects, 1 ≤ n ≤ 100000, and height h ≤ 1000; objects are not shared.
All leaf and intermediate values fit signed 64-bit integers; arithmetic and tag/child access take constant time.

options.text: Evaluate each child, discard those results, then evaluate both children again to obtain the subtraction result.
options.feedback: This still computes the correct expression, but it repeats complete child evaluations unnecessarily.

options.text: Add all leaves in the left subtree and subtract all leaves in the right subtree of the root.
options.feedback: SUB(10,SUB(7,2)) needs 10 minus (7 minus 2), so this produces 1 instead of 5.

options.text: For each SUB return the absolute difference of its two child values.
For a leaf return its value. For SUB, evaluate left and right once each, then return leftResult minus rightResult.
options.feedback: Each call implements the value contract and preserves which operand is subtracted.

feedback.reason: SUB requires left minus right, so save the left result while evaluating right.
details: Evaluate a leaf directly. At SUB, keep the returned left value while evaluating the right child, then subtract right from left. No subtree is evaluated more than once per occurrence.

SUB requires left minus right, so save the left result while evaluating right. Swapping evaluation results changes the value even though every leaf is still visited. One scalar per unfinished operator is sufficient.

“Evaluate each child, discard those results, then evaluate both children again to obtain the subtraction result.”: This still computes the correct expression, but it repeats complete child evaluations unnecessarily.
“Add all leaves in the left subtree and subtract all leaves in the right subtree of the root.”: SUB(10,SUB(7,2)) needs 10 minus (7 minus 2), so this produces 1 instead of 5.
“For each SUB return the absolute difference of its two child values.”: SUB(2,7) must return -5, not 5.

“For a leaf return its value. For SUB, evaluate left and right once each, then return leftResult minus rightResult.”: Each call implements the value contract and preserves which operand is subtracted.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze method-1 as described in the revealed method. Let n and h have the meanings in Q1. Use child indices and references without copying lists. Count active call frames; exclude input and returned output. There is no tail-call elimination. No hashing is used. Choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair among the options.

feedback.reason: Evaluate each expression occurrence once with constant state per active level.
details: Each expression object contributes constant local work. Pending operators retain a constant amount per active level.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Nested calls remain active along a path; their storage must be counted.
“O(n²) time, O(h + 1) auxiliary space”: Each object is processed once without rescanning or copying its descendants.
“O(h + 1) time, O(h + 1) auxiliary space”: A shallow but wide input can still require inspecting every object.
